title: Employment Situation (Dec 2026 data) — 08:30 ET, the December-boundary release that lands one session after the January coupon announcement and three before the block
source: BLS: bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm — table row "December 2026 | Jan. 08, 2027 | 08:30 AM" (BLS now lists a 2027 schedule; the 2026-09-09 fetch of 2027_sched.htm was a 404), same page lists January 2027 at Feb. 05, 2027, checked 2026-11-09. Promoted from EST: by the trigger the 2026-09-09 research set: the primary names the date that research derived
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN never-assessed RESEARCH (2026-09-09), superseding proposals/jobs-2027-01-08.from-treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-07.json, which stays where it is and is now shadowed. WHAT THIS SESSION ESTABLISHED THAT THE PROPOSAL DID NOT. (1) THE DATE IS RIGHT AND THE PROPOSAL'S REASON FOR IT IS WRONG. The proposal attributed the slip to New Year's Day and rested it on three holiday twins (2010-01-08, 2016-01-08, 2021-01-08), 3 for 3. The holiday is incidental. The real rule is a DECEMBER-REFERENCE BOUNDARY at January 4, it fires on non-holiday Fridays too, and it has fourteen instances and no counterexample since 1993 — which upgrades the date's support rather than weakening it. (2) THE SAME HOLIDAY MOVES THE OTHER WAY IN JULY, SO 'HOLIDAY SLIP' WAS NEVER ONE MECHANISM. When the rule lands on Independence Day the release moves ONE DAY EARLIER, to the Thursday: 1997-07-03 and 1998-07-02 in BLS's own historical release-date table, and 2026-07-02 on BLS's current schedule page. December moves a week later; July moves a day earlier. The likely reason December cannot move earlier is that the alternative would publish December data on 2026-12-31, inside the reference month — stated as an inference, not as a sourced fact. (3) THE SIBLING LEDGER'S SECOND-FRIDAY POPULATION IS MATERIALLY INCOMPLETE. jobs-2027-10-08 stated that second-Friday payrolls number 33-34 and are structurally impossible in January. On the corrected series they number 49, and JANUARY IS THE SINGLE LARGEST SOURCE at 14 — by release month {Jan 14, Feb 1, Mar 13, May 5, Jul 5, Oct 5, Dec 6}. The boundary rule is precisely what manufactures them: every slipped January release is a second Friday (7 days to opex), every on-time one is a first Friday (14 days). (4) THE RUNWAY EFFECT IS REAL, SMALLER THAN THE SIBLING MEASURED, AND STILL ARITHMETIC. Recomputed on the corrected 49-observation set, the print's share of realised variance from the print through same-month opex is SPY 17.5% against 6.4% (2.74x, P=0.0008), against the sibling's 3.76x on its 33; a length-matched five-session control drops the residual to 1.53x (P=0.204), further into the null than the sibling's own 1.96x (P=0.085). Per-session vol inside the window is unchanged (SPY 0.89x, P=0.27) and the print's own |move| is unchanged (SPY 1.01x, P=1.00). Adding the observations the plain rule could not see deflates the headline and strengthens the sibling's conclusion. (5) JANUARY IS A FOURTH SEASONAL PROFILE AND IT IS THE FLAT ONE. Payroll-day amplification (a month's payroll-session median |move| over that same month's non-payroll median), Yahoo split/dividend-adjusted bars 1993-2026: SPY 1.21x rank 8/12, QQQ 1.07x 9/12, TLT 1.14x 11/12, IEF 1.32x 8/12, SHY 1.51x 9/12, LQD 1.45x 7/12, AGG 1.58x 7/12, ^VIX 1.34x 7/12, HYG 1.29x 3/12. Eight of nine sit at or below their own median month and nothing ranks above 7th except credit. Against August's rates sweep (TLT/IEF/AGG 1/1/1) and October's equity-side/rates-last split, January amplifies nothing anywhere. (6) THE AUCTION-CORRIDOR CHANNEL THE PROPOSER CARED ABOUT DOES NOT SHOW UP IN THE TAPE. Restricting to the literal shape — a 3-Year note auctioned at exactly D+1, n=40 from Treasury's own auctions_query, January members 2015-01-09, 2021-01-08 and 2026-01-09 — D+1..D+3 realised vol is TLT 0.86x (P=0.435), IEF 0.87x (P=0.298), AGG 1.06x (P=0.648), SPY 0.87x (P=0.337). The broader 'two or more block auctions in the next five sessions' set (n=201) is null on every duration leg. (7) COORDINATES: ism-manufacturing-2027-01-05 at D-3, ism-services-2027-01-07 and treasury-coupon-announcement-2027-01-07 at D-1, treasury-3y-note-2027-01-11 at D+3, eia-steo-2027-01-12 and treasury-10y-note-2027-01-12 at D+4, treasury-30y-bond-2027-01-13 at D+5, opex-2027-01-15 at D+7, fomc-blackout-start-2027-01-16 at D+8, fomc-2027-01-27 at D+19. All eleven already carry researched ledgers. From federalreserve.gov's 2027 calendar re-fetched this session (HTTP 200, page-stated 'Last Update: August 19, 2026'), the 2027 meetings are January 26-27, March 16-17*, April 27-28, June 8-9*, July 27-28, September 14-15*, October 26-27 and December 7-8*; with the next release at 2027-02-05 this is the LAST payroll the January 26-27 meeting sees. HONEST LIMITS. Status is estimate and stays there; impact high and symbols [] match every other jobs-* entry; nothing here licenses an entry. The January release is also the last before the CES annual benchmark revision cycle, which this session did not source and therefore does not claim.
